text:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding gpt-mid-8k-v2 weights to s3://redwood-models/gpt-mid-8k-v2/prod. Noticing tokenizer deltas vs gpt-mid-8k-v1. Can the runtime/tokenizer folks confirm expected BOS/EOS behavior and chat-template mapping? Quick example below.

maria: Example tokenizations I dumped: 
```
prompt:
[system] You are helpful.
[user] Hi!

v1 tokens: [50256, 174, 11, 198, 50257]    # v1 had implicit BOS removed upstream
v2 tokens: [1, 50256, 174, 11, 198, 50257]  # v2 prepends a  token (id=1)
```

maria: Also seeing that v2's tokenizer exposes a special <|system|> token in the tokenizer vocab which v1 didn't. Not sure if we should map that to the 'system' chat role in our chat template or keep it literal.

jack: quick look — @maria is that dump from the raw tokenizer or after our preproc layer?

maria: raw tokenizer output. I didn't run our serving preproc yet. Wanted to surface before we flip weights.

anita: I've hit this before with another model family. v2 seems to be a byte-level BPE that explicitly outputs a BOS token (id=1). v1 relied on the client to add/strip BOS. Two viable options:
- set tokenizer_config.add_bos = false for serving (strip at tokenization time)
- keep add_bos=true and update preproc to expect leading BOS and adjust templates
Either is fine but must match eval prompts so metrics don't jump.

lucas: also check model.config.json: sometimes eos_token is null vs numeric id. If eos_token is missing we default to 50256, which can shift how we post-process. Quick grep: `jq .eos_token model.config.json` on the weights tar.

priya: I'm going to open a tiny PR to runtime-configs with a validator that checks: presence of bos_token/eos_token, whether tokenizer.add_bos is set, and a mapping table for chat roles -> special tokens. Will tag this thread.

maria: thanks @priya. For the chat template question: v2 has explicit tokens for <|system|>, <|user|>, <|assistant|>. Should those be inserted by the serving runtime (preserve roles) or left in the prompt strings? My worry: some older clients were relying on our runtime to synthesize role markers.

jack: prefer runtime to synthesize role markers (keep client simple). But we must document: if tokenizer has explicit role tokens, runtime should map 'system' -> <|system|> (and not emit extra textual markers). Also add a compatibility toggle.

anita: agreed. Implementation note: when constructing the final token sequence we should dedupe adjacent special tokens. Eg if client already sent a leading <|system|> we shouldn't add another.

lucas: small nit — if we choose to strip BOS in preproc, ensure the KV cache indexing stays consistent. Some of our attention-kernel code assumes cache index 0 is the first model token after any BOS. If we remove BOS there needs to be an off-by-one check in the cache offset logic.

priya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime-configs/pull/482 — adds: tokenizer schema validation, a compatibility flag `tokenizer.lead_bos_mode` (values: keep|strip|normalize), and an example chat-mapping file. Please review.

maria: awesome. I'll run the v2 eval suite once changes land. Can someone from eng-runtime do a quick review of the KV off-by-one risk? @lucas @jack

lucas: on it, will run a small end-to-end with a short chat and inspect kv indexes and cached key lengths.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: config PR touched. CI: 14 checks passing, 0 failing. Staging deploy scheduled at 2025-12-12T22:15Z if approved.

jack: tagging @anita for tokenizer tests and @priya for validation bits. If we get tests green today we can flip weights in staging and sanity-check latency + token counts.

anita: will add a unit test that compares token counts for canonical prompts (with/without explicit role tokens) and flags >2 token delta.

maria: thanks all. I'll hold off on promoting to prod until we confirm: tokenizer.lead_bos_mode, mapping file present, and KV cache check passes.

jack: sounds good. Ping this thread when staging flip is done. :thumbsup:
